name: StanceThemeProvider
summary: Applies the Stance theme at the app root, persists the preference and avoids a wrong-theme flash at launch.
accessibility: System mode follows the colour scheme and Increase Contrast
Preference is read before the first frame

name: stanceTheme(_:)
summary: Modifier that applies a Stance appearance (system, light, dark or high contrast) to a view hierarchy.
accessibility: Sets tint, foreground and canvas background from tokens

name: stanceScopedTheme(_:)
summary: Scopes a fixed theme to a subtree, for inverted sections and side-by-side previews.
accessibility: Scoped themes keep the same verified contrast as page themes

name: StanceAppearance
summary: The appearance preference with the same stored values as the web: system, light, dark and high-contrast.
accessibility: Increase Contrast resolves system mode to high contrast

name: StanceCard
summary: A padded surface with optional title, description and footer for grouped, self-contained content.
accessibility: Title is exposed as a heading

name: stanceCard()
summary: Modifier that gives any view the card treatment: padding, surface colour, border and optional elevation.
accessibility: High contrast replaces the shadow with a solid outline

name: stanceSurface()
summary: Modifier that places a view on a token surface level with a corner radius, border and optional shadow.
accessibility: Boundaries meet 3:1 contrast in every theme

name: stanceShadow()
summary: Modifier that adds a token elevation; high contrast draws depth as an outline instead of a blur.
accessibility: Depth never relies on subtle shading in high contrast

name: StanceDivider
summary: A hairline separator in the theme separator colour, horizontal or vertical, hidden from VoiceOver.
accessibility: Decorative: hidden from assistive technology

name: StanceSection
summary: A titled group of content with consistent spacing and an optional caption under the heading.
example: StanceSection("Details", caption: "Shown to your organisation") { Text("Body") }
accessibility: Title is exposed as a heading for rotor navigation

name: StanceContainer
summary: Constrains content to a readable width with page gutters and centres it on iPad.
accessibility: Keeps line length readable at every size class

name: StanceGrid
summary: An adaptive grid that fits as many columns as the minimum item width allows.
accessibility: Reflows to one column at large text sizes

name: StanceIcon
summary: A Stance icon drawn natively from the shared icon geometry; decorative unless a label is given.
accessibility: Hidden from VoiceOver without a label
Scales with Dynamic Type

name: stanceText(_:)
summary: Modifier that applies a semantic Stance text style which scales with Dynamic Type and Bold Text.
accessibility: Scales through the largest accessibility sizes
Never below 12pt at the default size

name: StanceButton
summary: A button with six variants, three sizes, icons, a pill shape and a loading state that blocks repeat taps.
accessibility: 44pt minimum target at every size
Loading is announced as “In progress”

name: StanceButtonStyle
summary: The Stance button style for any Button, Menu label or NavigationLink: .buttonStyle(.stance(.primary)).
accessibility: Press feedback respects Reduce Motion

name: StanceIconButton
summary: An icon-only button that requires an accessibility label and keeps a 44pt touch target.
accessibility: Label is required and used by VoiceOver and Voice Control
Pointer hover effect on iPad

name: StanceButtonGroup
summary: Lays related buttons out in a row and stacks them vertically at accessibility text sizes.
accessibility: Reflows instead of truncating at large text sizes

name: StanceMenu
summary: The native Menu with a Stance button as its trigger, for short lists of actions.
accessibility: System menu behaviour, VoiceOver and keyboard support

name: StanceFormField
summary: Wires a visible label, helper text and an announced error message to a single control.
accessibility: Label becomes the control’s accessibility label
Errors are announced when they appear

name: StanceTextField
summary: A labelled single-line text field with helper text, error state, required marker and leading icon.
example: StanceTextField("Template name", text: $text, helper: "Visible to your organisation", isRequired: true)
accessibility: Visible label matches the accessibility label for Voice Control
Error replaces the helper in the hint

name: StanceSecureField
summary: A password field with a show and hide control that keeps a 44pt target.
accessibility: Toggle is labelled Show password or Hide password

name: StanceTextEditor
summary: A labelled multi-line editor with an optional live character count.
accessibility: Character count is part of the field hint

name: StanceSearchField
summary: An inline search field with a clear button; use the system searchable modifier for screen-level search.
accessibility: Clear button is labelled and reachable

name: StancePicker
summary: A labelled native Picker shown as a menu inside Stance field chrome.
accessibility: Selected value is exposed as the accessibility value

name: StanceCheckbox
summary: A checkbox with a label and description; iOS has no system checkbox, so it is exposed as a toggle.
example: StanceCheckbox("Apply to new members", description: "Added later", isOn: $isOn)
accessibility: Whole row is the 44pt target
Announces Checked or Not checked

name: StanceRadioGroup
summary: A group of mutually exclusive options visible at once, with optional descriptions.
accessibility: Selected option carries the selected trait
Group is labelled by its title

name: StanceToggleStyle
summary: Stance colours for the native Toggle switch, keeping system behaviour and accessibility.
accessibility: Native switch semantics and haptics

name: StanceSlider
summary: A labelled native Slider that reports a formatted value visually and to VoiceOver.
accessibility: Adjustable trait with a readable value

name: StanceDatePicker
summary: A labelled native DatePicker for dates or times in Stance colours.
accessibility: System picker with full VoiceOver and keyboard support

name: StanceAdaptiveNavigation
summary: Top-level navigation that is a tab bar in compact width and a sidebar in regular width.
example: StanceAdaptiveNavigation("Stance", selection: $role, destinations: [.init(id: "admin", title: "Home", systemImage: "house")]) { _ in Text("Home") }
accessibility: System bars keep their materials, including Liquid Glass on iOS 26

name: stanceNavigationChrome()
summary: Modifier that themes navigation and tab bar tint while leaving system bar materials untouched.
accessibility: Bar content stays legible in all three themes

name: StanceStepper
summary: Shows progress through a multi-step task with completed, current and upcoming steps.
accessibility: Each step reads “Step x of y” with its state

name: StancePageIndicator
summary: Dots that show the position in a short paged sequence.
accessibility: Read as “Page 2 of 4”
Animation respects Reduce Motion

name: StanceBadge
summary: A short status label in a neutral, info, success, warning or danger tone, always with text.
accessibility: Never colour alone
Outlined in high contrast

name: StanceTag
summary: A keyword label with an optional remove button labelled with the tag name.
accessibility: Remove button reads “Remove Sales”

name: StanceAvatar
summary: A person or organisation shown as an image or initials, in three sizes.
accessibility: Name is the accessibility label

name: StanceAvatarGroup
summary: Overlapping avatars with a +N overflow, read as one summary by VoiceOver.
accessibility: Reads names followed by “and N more”

name: StanceProgressView
summary: Linear or circular progress in Stance colours, determinate or indeterminate.
accessibility: Label and percentage are exposed to VoiceOver

name: StanceSkeleton
summary: A placeholder for loading content in text, circle or rectangle shapes; static under Reduce Motion.
accessibility: Hidden from VoiceOver

name: StanceEmptyState
summary: Explains an empty screen or list and offers the next action.
example: StanceEmptyState(title: "No templates yet", message: "Create your first signature template.") { StanceButton("New template") {} }
accessibility: Title is a heading

name: StanceTimeline
summary: A vertical sequence of events with a title, detail, time and tone.
example: StanceTimeline([.init(id: "1", title: "Deployed", detail: "48 mailboxes", time: "09:41", tone: .success)])
accessibility: Each event is one combined element

name: StanceStatCard
summary: A key figure with a label and a change that is described in words for VoiceOver.
accessibility: Reads “up 12% from last month”, not just an arrow

name: StanceDescriptionList
summary: Term and detail pairs that stack vertically at accessibility text sizes.
accessibility: Each pair is read together

name: StanceListRow
summary: A list row with leading content, title, subtitle and trailing accessory for List and NavigationLink.
accessibility: 44pt minimum row height

name: stanceListStyle()
summary: Modifiers that put List and Form on the Stance canvas with themed rows and separators.
accessibility: Keeps native list behaviour, swipe actions and editing

name: StanceDisclosureGroupStyle
summary: Stance styling for the native DisclosureGroup with a 44pt header.
accessibility: Announces Expanded or Collapsed

name: StanceInlineAlert
summary: An inline status message with a tone icon, title, message and optional actions.
example: StanceInlineAlert("Relay offline", message: "Deployments will resume.", tone: .warning)
accessibility: Warning and danger tones are announced when shown

name: StanceBanner
summary: A full-width announcement with an optional action and dismiss button.
example: StanceBanner("Maintenance on Sunday", actionTitle: "Details", action: {}, onDismiss: {})
accessibility: Dismiss button is labelled and 44pt

name: StanceToastCenter
summary: Queues transient messages, shows one at a time and announces each to VoiceOver.
accessibility: Announced without moving focus
Manual dismiss always available

name: StanceLoadingState
summary: A centred progress indicator with a message for loading screens and regions.
accessibility: Indicator and message are one element

name: StanceErrorState
summary: Explains a failure in plain language and offers a retry action.
example: StanceErrorState(message: "We could not load your templates.") {}
accessibility: Title is a heading; retry is a labelled button

name: stanceSheet()
summary: Presents the native sheet with a title bar, detents and themed content.
accessibility: System sheet gestures, grabber and focus handling

name: stanceAlert()
summary: Presents the system alert from a typed confirmation, with a destructive option.
accessibility: System alert semantics and focus

name: stanceConfirmationDialog()
summary: Presents the system confirmation dialog: an action sheet on iPhone and a popover on iPad.
accessibility: Cancel is always available

name: StanceFilterBar
summary: A horizontally scrolling row of selectable filter chips with a clear-all action.
accessibility: Selected chips carry the selected trait and a check mark

name: StanceSearchableList
summary: A list with native search that filters as you type and announces the result count.
accessibility: Result count is announced
Empty state explains what to try

name: StanceCalendar
summary: A month calendar built on the native graphical DatePicker in Stance colours.
accessibility: Full system calendar accessibility

name: StanceSignatureCanvas
summary: A canvas for drawing a signature with a finger or Apple Pencil, with undo, clear and an alternative slot.
example: StanceSignatureCanvas(signature: $signature) { StanceTextField("Or type your name", text: $text) }
accessibility: Direct-touch trait for VoiceOver
Offer the typed alternative for people who cannot draw

name: StanceAttachmentPicker
summary: Buttons that open the system photo picker and file importer without requesting library permission.
accessibility: System pickers are fully accessible

name: StanceDocumentPreview
summary: Previews a local PDF, image or document with the system Quick Look viewer (iOS only).
accessibility: Quick Look provides zoom, VoiceOver and text selection

name: stanceTouchTarget()
summary: Modifier that guarantees the 44 by 44 point minimum interactive target without changing visual size.
accessibility: Apple HIG minimum target

name: StanceUIKit
summary: UIKit access to Stance: dynamic UIColor roles, Dynamic Type UIFonts and a themed hosting controller.
accessibility: Dynamic colours follow dark mode and Increase Contrast

name: StanceHaptics
summary: Haptic feedback helpers for selection, success, warning and error; no-ops where unavailable.
accessibility: Haptics supplement, never replace, visible feedback

name: StanceRangeSlider
summary: Two thumbs on one track choose a lower and an upper value, each adjustable on its own with VoiceOver.
accessibility: Each thumb is a separate adjustable element named by the label and its role
Thumbs mirror in right to left layouts like the system slider
The range is spoken as words, for example 1,000 to 5,000

name: StancePinField
summary: Boxes for a short verification code over one real text field, so autofill from Messages and paste fill every box.
accessibility: VoiceOver reads one text field, not separate boxes
Masked codes report how many characters are entered instead of the characters
The code reads left to right in every language

name: StanceNumberField
summary: A number field with locale formatting, bounds and the system Stepper. Bind an optional Double to allow an empty field.
example: StanceNumberField("Licence seats", value: $value, min: 1, max: 500, suffix: "seats")
accessibility: The system stepper adjusts with VoiceOver swipes
Prefix and suffix are read with the value
An empty optional field reads as Empty

name: StanceCombobox
summary: Opens a searchable system list in a sheet or popover and picks one value, or accepts typed text as a new value.
example: StanceCombobox("Team", selection: $selection, options: [.init("sales", label: "Sales"), .init("legal", label: "Legal")], custom: .text)
accessibility: The field reads its label and the chosen value
The chosen row carries the selected trait
Typed text that matches no option is offered as the first row, and Return commits it

name: StanceMultiSelect
summary: Picks several values from a searchable list and shows each choice below the field as a removable tag.
example: StanceMultiSelect("Departments", selection: $filters, options: [.init("sales", label: "Sales"), .init("legal", label: "Legal")], custom: .text)
accessibility: The field reads every chosen value as a list
Each tag has a remove button named after its value
Typed text that matches no option can be created as a new tag

name: StanceCheckboxGroup
summary: A short list of checkboxes under one heading, with helper or error text and an optional select all.
example: StanceCheckboxGroup("Notify by", selection: $filters, options: [.init("email", label: "Email"), .init("push", label: "Push")], showsSelectAll: true)
accessibility: The heading names the group as VoiceOver enters it
Select all reports checked, not checked or partly checked
Errors are announced when they appear

name: StanceDateRangePicker
summary: A start and an end date from two system date pickers, with presets and the span summarised in words.
accessibility: Each picker is named Start or End
The end date can never fall before the start date
The summary reads the range and its length as one line

name: StanceTimePicker
summary: A time of day from the system date picker, with the hour cycle and digits following the locale.
accessibility: The system picker reads the label and the time
Compact and wheel styles both keep a 44pt target

name: StanceInlineEdit
summary: Text that becomes a text field when tapped. Return saves, cancel or Escape restores the earlier value.
accessibility: The row reads its label and value with a hint that it can be edited
Save and cancel are labelled buttons with 44pt targets
Validation errors are announced

name: StanceDataTable
summary: Sortable rows with selection: the system Table on iPad, a pinned header grid before iOS 17.4 and cards on iPhone.
accessibility: Compact cards and grid rows read every column name with its value
Selected rows carry the selected trait
Headers are headers and speak their sort direction

name: StancePagination
summary: Previous and next buttons with a page summary, and a steady row of page numbers when the width allows.
accessibility: The new page is announced after each move
The current page carries the selected trait
Labels give way to icons at accessibility text sizes

name: StanceTreeView
summary: Nested folders or teams in a List, with expansion you control, selection and level information for VoiceOver.
example: StanceTreeView(nodes: [StanceTreeNode(id: "templates", title: "Templates", children: [StanceTreeNode(id: "sales", title: "Sales signature")])], expanded: .constant(["templates"]), selection: $selection)
accessibility: Each row reads its level, position and expanded state
Expand and collapse are VoiceOver actions
Chevrons point the right way in right to left layouts

name: StanceSortableList
summary: A List people reorder by dragging the system handles or with Move up and Move down actions in VoiceOver.
example: StanceSortableList("Approval steps", items: .constant([ComponentExamples.Named(name: "Legal"), ComponentExamples.Named(name: "Finance")]), itemLabel: \.name) { Text($0.name) }
accessibility: Move up and Move down actions need no drag
Each move is announced with the new position
Rows read their position in the list

name: StanceChart
summary: Line, bar or area chart on Swift Charts in ink tones, with a spoken summary, Audio Graphs and a table view.
accessibility: VoiceOver reads a summary with the highest and lowest values
Audio Graphs through an accessibility chart descriptor
Series differ by symbol and dash, not colour alone

name: StanceRichText
summary: Turns Markdown into headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes and code, set in the Stance type scale.
example: StanceRichText(markdown: "## Rollout\nSignatures deploy **after** the next sync.")
accessibility: Headings carry the header trait for the rotor
Links use the link colour and an underline
Text scales with Dynamic Type

name: StanceCodeBlock
summary: Monospaced code with ink scale syntax highlighting, optional line numbers, sideways scrolling and a copy button.
accessibility: Highlighting uses weight, italics and underline as well as ink, never hue alone
Line numbers are hidden from VoiceOver and the code stays selectable
Code stays left to right in right to left layouts

name: StanceProgressCircle
summary: A ring that fills with progress and shows the percentage inside, built on the system ProgressView.
accessibility: Read as progress with its label and percentage
Every size keeps a 44pt frame
A success haptic plays when it completes

name: StanceAccordion
summary: Stacks collapsible sections on DisclosureGroup, with one or many open at a time and an optional card for each.
example: StanceAccordion([StanceAccordionSection(id: "billing", title: "Billing")], expanded: $filters, mode: .single) { _ in Text("Invoices go out on the first of the month.") }
accessibility: Each title is a header and a button that reports expanded or collapsed
Disabled sections cannot be toggled
Opening and closing follow Reduce Motion

name: StanceTabs
summary: Switches views within one screen, as the system segmented control or a scrolling underline strip with counts.
example: StanceTabs([StanceTab(id: "admin", title: "Details"), StanceTab(id: "member", title: "Activity", badge: 3)], selection: $role) { Text($0) }
accessibility: Each tab reads its position, such as Tab 2 of 4
The selected tab carries the selected trait
The strip scrolls the selected tab into view

name: StanceCopyButton
summary: Puts text on the pasteboard, then briefly shows a tick with a spoken confirmation and a success haptic.
accessibility: Copied is announced without moving focus
Icon only buttons keep Copy as their name
The confirmation reverts on its own after a moment

name: StanceSplitButton
summary: Pairs a main action with a menu of related ones, using the system menu with a primary action plus a chevron.
accessibility: VoiceOver hears the action and a separate More options button
A hint explains touch and hold
Both segments keep a 44pt target

name: StanceToggleButton
summary: A button that stays pressed while its option is on, drawn from the native Toggle with a filled selected look.
accessibility: The on state carries the selected trait
On is shown by fill, border and weight, not colour alone
A selection tick plays when it changes

name: StanceToggleButtonGroup
summary: Related toggle buttons for one setting, as a single or multiple choice, wrapping onto new lines at large sizes.
example: StanceToggleButtonGroup("Channels", selection: $filters, options: [StanceToggleOption("email", title: "Email"), StanceToggleOption("sms", title: "SMS")])
accessibility: The group is named by its label
Each option reports whether it is selected
Buttons reflow instead of truncating

name: StanceChip
summary: A small rounded value people can tap or remove, such as a recipient or a condition already applied.
accessibility: The remove button is named after the value
Remove keeps a 44pt touch area around a small icon
A chip without an action reads as plain text

name: StanceFilterChip
summary: An on or off chip for a row of filters, with a tick and an optional match count once applied.
accessibility: The applied state carries the selected trait
The tick means status is never shown by colour alone
A selection tick plays when it changes

name: StanceNotificationRow
summary: One notice with its time and unread dot, plus swipe and VoiceOver actions to mark it read or delete it.
example: List { StanceNotificationRow("Deployment finished", message: "48 mailboxes updated", time: "2 min ago", isUnread: true, onDelete: {}) }
accessibility: Unread is spoken before the title
Swipe actions are also VoiceOver custom actions
Text reflows at accessibility sizes

name: StanceThread
summary: The scrolling container for a conversation. Follows the latest message while the reader is at the bottom and releases when they scroll up.
accessibility: A labelled container for the conversation
Never moves the reader while they are scrolled up
Scroll to latest button keeps a 44pt target

name: StanceMessage
summary: One turn in a conversation from the user, the assistant or the system, with slots for actions and a footer.
example: StanceMessage(role: .assistant, status: .streaming, author: "Assistant") { StanceStreamingText(text, isStreaming: true) }
accessibility: Named by author and time
Status is exposed as a value and marked as updating while streaming
The assistant is identified by the sparkle and its name, never by colour

name: StanceMessageGroup
summary: Runs of messages from one author gathered under a single avatar and name, so the thread reads calmly.
accessibility: The group is named by its author
The avatar is decorative

name: StanceMessageActions
summary: Copy, retry, edit and rating buttons in a row beneath a message, each with a clear VoiceOver name.
example: StanceMessageActions(rating: rating, onCopy: {}, onRetry: {}, onRate: { rating = $0 })
accessibility: Every button has a name and a 44pt target
Rating buttons are toggles with a selected state
Copy confirms with a polite announcement
Wraps onto more lines at large text sizes

name: StanceBranchSwitcher
summary: Moves between the alternative versions of a message that an edit or a retry produced.
accessibility: Previous and next buttons are named and disabled at the ends
The position is read as "Version 2 of 3" and announced when it changes
Chevrons mirror in right to left layouts

name: StanceScrollToLatest
summary: A floating button that shows up once the reader scrolls away from the newest message and jumps back.
accessibility: Named "Scroll to latest" with the unread count as its value
44pt target
Fades without movement under Reduce Motion

name: StanceConversationList
summary: A list of past conversations grouped by date, with selection, rename, pin and delete.
example: StanceConversationList([StanceConversation(id: "1", title: "Budget review", updatedAt: date)], selection: $selection, onDelete: { _ in })
accessibility: The open conversation has the selected trait
Rename, pin and delete are swipe actions and context menu items
Section headers name each date group

name: StanceThreadEmptyState
summary: The first screen of a fresh conversation, with a greeting and a few starter prompts to tap.
example: StanceThreadEmptyState(description: "Ask about your documents.", starters: [StanceStarter(id: "1", label: "Summarise a file")]) { _ in }
accessibility: The greeting is a heading
Starters are full width buttons with 44pt targets

name: StancePromptComposer
summary: The message input. A text field that grows with its content, with slots for attachments, tools and the send or stop button.
accessibility: A labelled group with a labelled field
Send is disabled when the draft is empty
While a response is generated the same button is named Stop
Controls move below the field at accessibility text sizes

name: StanceAttachmentTray
summary: The attachments on a draft or a sent message: files and images with progress, errors and remove.
accessibility: Each remove button names its file
Upload errors are announced and shown with an icon and text
Becomes a column at accessibility text sizes

name: StanceMentionPicker
summary: A filterable list that opens from a trigger character to reference files, people or tools.
example: StanceMentionPicker(isPresented: $isPresented, query: text, items: [StanceSuggestion(id: "1", label: "Budget.xlsx")]) { _ in }
accessibility: A labelled list above the composer; focus stays in the field
Escape and the VoiceOver escape gesture close it
The number of matches is announced

name: StanceSlashCommandMenu
summary: A command list that opens when the draft starts with a slash.
example: StanceSlashCommandMenu(isPresented: $isPresented, query: text, commands: [StanceSlashCommand(id: "1", name: "summarise")]) { _ in }
accessibility: Same list pattern as the mention picker
Escape and the VoiceOver escape gesture close it

name: StanceModelPicker
summary: A system menu for choosing the model behind the next message, with a short line and capability badges.
accessibility: The system menu, with its own tick and VoiceOver behaviour
The chosen model is the value

name: StanceContextChips
summary: Shows what the assistant can see for this message, such as files, pages or selections, each removable.
example: StanceContextChips([StanceContextItem(id: "1", label: "budget.xlsx", icon: .file, kind: "File")], onRemove: { _ in }, onAdd: {})
accessibility: Each remove button names its item
The kind is read before the label
Chips wrap instead of truncating the row

name: StanceVoiceInputButton
summary: A microphone button with idle, listening and processing states and a level indicator.
accessibility: A toggle button with the state as its value
State changes are announced
The level ring is still under Reduce Motion

name: StanceStopButton
summary: Stops a response that is being generated.
accessibility: Named "Stop"
44pt target at every size

name: StanceTokenBudgetMeter
summary: A compact meter of how much of the context or message limit is used, with a warning near the limit.
accessibility: One element with the value in words
The warning is an icon and text, never colour alone
Crossing the warning threshold and the limit is announced once each

name: StanceStreamingText
summary: Reveals text as it arrives at a steady cadence with an optional caret, without reflowing what is already on screen.
accessibility: VoiceOver gets the text once, when it is complete, never token by token
Text appears at once under Reduce Motion
Never takes focus

name: StanceThinkingIndicator
summary: Shows that the assistant is working before any text arrives, with an optional label and elapsed time.
accessibility: The label is announced once when it appears
A still sparkle with the label under Reduce Motion
Elapsed time is the value

name: StanceReasoningDisclosure
summary: A collapsible block for the assistant's reasoning. Open while thinking, collapsed to a summary when done.
accessibility: A button with its expanded state
The summary reads, for example, "Thought for 12 seconds"

name: StanceShimmerText
summary: A label with a slow sweep of light for work in progress, such as searching, and still under Reduce Motion.
accessibility: Plain text to assistive technology
No animation under Reduce Motion
The sweep follows the reading direction

name: StanceGenerationProgress
summary: Progress for longer generations such as images or documents: determinate or indeterminate, with a stage label.
accessibility: One element with the percentage and stage as its value
Stage changes are announced politely
A success haptic when it completes

name: StanceStreamingSkeleton
summary: Placeholder lines for a response that has been requested and has not started.
accessibility: One element named "Loading response"
Still under Reduce Motion

name: StanceInterruptedState
summary: Flags a response that stopped or failed part way through and offers retry and continue.
accessibility: Errors and lost connections are announced as alerts; stopped and limit are polite
The reason is an icon and words, never colour alone

name: StanceCitationChip
summary: An inline numbered marker that links a claim to its source and previews it on tap.
example: StanceCitationChip(index: 2, source: StanceSource(id: "1", title: "Quarterly report", url: URL(string: "https://example.com")))
accessibility: Named "Source 2: title"
The preview is a popover on iPad and a sheet on iPhone
44pt target around a small mark

name: StanceSourceList
summary: The sources behind an answer, as a compact row that expands to a full list.
accessibility: The compact row is a button with its expanded state
Each row is a link named by number, title and site

name: StanceSourcePreview
summary: A card for one source: title, site, snippet and a link to open it.
example: StanceSourcePreview(StanceSource(id: "1", title: "Quarterly report", domain: "example.com", snippet: "Revenue grew 12%."))
accessibility: The open control is a link
Text wraps instead of truncating at regular size

name: StanceConfidenceBadge
summary: States how sure the system is in words, never colour alone.
accessibility: The level is always written out
The bars icon is decorative

name: StanceAIGeneratedLabel
summary: Marks content as written or edited by AI.
accessibility: Read as one phrase
Identified by the sparkle and words, not a hue

name: StanceDisclaimerNote
summary: A quiet line under the composer or a reply, such as a reminder to check important facts.
accessibility: Muted text still meets contrast in every theme
The icon is decorative

name: StanceFeedbackBar
summary: Thumbs up or down, then optional reasons and a comment, ending with a short thank you.
accessibility: Thumbs are toggle buttons
Reasons are a labelled group of toggles
Submission is announced

name: StanceReportDialog
summary: A sheet to report a response with a category and details.
example: Button("Report") { isPresented = true }.stanceReportDialog(isPresented: $isPresented, categories: [StanceReportCategory(id: "wrong", label: "Incorrect")]) { _ in }
accessibility: The system sheet with its own dismissal gestures
Submit is disabled until a category is chosen
Stays open and busy while the report is sent, then announces it

name: StanceSensitiveContentGate
summary: Keeps content behind a notice until the reader decides to reveal it.
accessibility: Hidden content is not in the accessibility tree
VoiceOver focus moves to the content on reveal

name: StanceInlineSuggestion
summary: A text field that shows a completion as muted ghost text after the caret, accepted from the keyboard bar or with Tab.
example: StanceInlineSuggestion("Reply", text: $text, suggestion: "Thanks for the update")
accessibility: A new suggestion is announced once with how to accept it
Accept and dismiss are VoiceOver actions on the field
The ghost text is never part of the field value

name: StanceSmartField
summary: Wraps any form control and states in words when its value was suggested, from which source, with use, undo and retry.
example: StanceSmartField("City", status: .suggested, suggestedValue: "Ljubljana", suggestionSource: "Invoice 114", onAccept: {}) { TextField("", text: $text) }
accessibility: The suggested and filled in states are text, not a colour
Undo and apply are announced
Still text replaces the shimmer under Reduce Motion

name: StanceRewriteMenu
summary: A system menu of text changes with nested tone choices, an optional typed instruction and a reviewable result card.
example: StanceRewriteMenu(onAction: { _ in }) { Text("Shorter text") } onAcceptPreview: {} onDiscardPreview: {}
accessibility: The system menu handles focus, submenus and dismissal
The result is a labelled region with Replace and Discard
Replace and discard are announced with a haptic

name: StanceSummaryCard
summary: Key points of a longer item in a card that carries the AI label, lists its sources and links back to the original.
accessibility: The title is a heading and each point is one element
Started, finished and failed are announced once
Collapsing uses the system disclosure with its expanded state

name: StanceAskBar
summary: A one line question field for a page with suggested questions below and the answer appearing in place when ready.
example: StanceAskBar(text: $text, suggestions: [StanceSuggestionChip(id: "1", label: "Who approves travel?")]) { _ in }
accessibility: The field carries the search trait and a Search return key
Answer ready is announced once, never the stream
Clear and every suggestion keep a 44pt target

name: StanceSuggestionChips
summary: Tappable follow up prompts that wrap onto more lines at large text sizes, with placeholders while they load.
example: StanceSuggestionChips([StanceSuggestionChip(id: "1", label: "Show as a table", icon: .list)]) { _ in }
accessibility: The group has a name and each chip is a button
Chips wrap instead of truncating at large text sizes
Loading is one element named Loading suggestions

name: StanceInsightCallout
summary: Flags a finding in your data with its tone in words, the evidence in a disclosure, a confidence badge and one action.
example: StanceInsightCallout("Travel is 8% over plan", tone: .attention, actionTitle: "Review", action: {}) { Text("Two workshops were not forecast.") }
accessibility: Tone is an icon and an eyebrow in words on ink surfaces
Evidence expands with the system disclosure
Dismiss is a labelled 44pt button

name: StanceSemanticSearchResults
summary: Meaning based results that bold the matching passage and say the source, the match strength and the reason in words.
example: StanceSemanticSearchResults(query: "travel", results: [StanceSearchResult(id: "1", title: "Travel policy", snippet: "Trips over 400 EUR need approval.", highlights: ["approval"], score: 0.92)])
accessibility: The result count is announced once when loading ends
Highlights use weight and a tint, never colour alone
Only http and https links are opened

name: StanceCopilotPanel
summary: An assistant docked beside your page: the system inspector column on iPad and a sheet with detents on iPhone.
example: Button("Assistant") { isPresented = true }.stanceCopilotPanel(isPresented: $isPresented) { StanceCopilotPanel(onClose: { isPresented = false }) { Text("Thread") } }
accessibility: The panel is a named container with a heading
The system sheet keeps its own dismissal gestures on iPhone
Close is a labelled 44pt button

name: StanceMarkdownRenderer
summary: Turns model Markdown into native headings, lists, tables and highlighted code, and keeps its shape while text streams in.
example:
StanceMarkdownRenderer("## Summary

Travel is **up 8%** [1].

- [x] Compare versions", citations: [1: StanceSource(id: "q3", title: "Q3 budget review")], baseHeadingLevel: 2)
accessibility: Headings carry the header trait and a level that starts at a base you choose
Only http, https and mailto links can be followed; images show their alt text
Task items say checked or not checked, and table rows read each column name

name: StanceCodeSuggestion
summary: Generated code in a highlighted block with copy, apply and run buttons, and the run result stated in words below it.
example: StanceCodeSuggestion("let total = 1284", language: "swift", filename: "Budget.swift", isApplied: isOn, runStatus: .complete, runOutput: "1284", onApply: { isOn = true }, onRun: {})
accessibility: Applying is confirmed with a haptic and one announcement
The run result is text beside its icon and is announced once per change
Code and output stay left to right in right to left layouts

name: StanceArtifactPanel
summary: A side panel for a generated document or app with version and preview or code pickers: an inspector on iPad, a sheet on iPhone.
example: Button("Open") { isPresented = true }.stanceArtifactPanel(isPresented: $isPresented) { StanceArtifactPanel("Travel summary", kind: "Document", onClose: { isPresented = false }) { Text("Trips over 400 EUR need approval.") } }
accessibility: The panel is a region named after the artifact, with a header title
Version and view switches are system pickers with their own names
As a sheet, the system returns focus to the opener on close

name: StanceGeneratedImage
summary: Shows a generated picture your app supplies, holding its frame while it loads, with variations and the system share sheet.
example: StanceGeneratedImage(Image(systemName: "photo"), alt: "Grey hills under a pale sun", prompt: "Hills in ink", onRegenerate: {})
accessibility: Alt text is required and read as the image label
Loading is the system progress view with a label and value
The chosen variation has the selected trait and a tick, with its position

name: StanceGeneratedTable
summary: An assistant made table on StanceDataTable with a caption, numeric sorting, a row cap and one tap copy as CSV.
example: StanceGeneratedTable("Budget changes", columns: [StanceGeneratedTableColumn(id: "line", header: "Line"), StanceGeneratedTableColumn(id: "change", header: "Change", isNumeric: true)], rows: [StanceGeneratedTableRow(id: "1", ["line": "Travel", "change": "+8%"])], maxRows: 5)
accessibility: The caption is a header and the accessible name of the table
Rows that arrive while streaming are not announced one by one
Copying as CSV is announced and confirmed with a haptic

name: StanceGeneratedChart
summary: Wraps StanceChart for assistant made charts: a plain language takeaway, a chart or table switch and a note naming the source.
example: StanceGeneratedChart("Spend by line", takeaway: "Travel is the largest line.", series: [StanceChartSeries("FY27", points: [StanceChartPoint("Travel", 12400), StanceChartPoint("Software", 9800)])], source: "FY27 workbook")
accessibility: The takeaway is visible text and the alternative to the drawing
The same data is always one tap away as a table
The chart supports Audio Graphs through its chart descriptor

name: StanceFilePreviewCard
summary: A compact card for a file the assistant made or read, with kind, size, progress and Quick Look when it is opened.
example: StanceFilePreviewCard("Budget FY27.xlsx", size: 482_000, meta: "3 sheets", onOpen: {}, onDownload: {})
accessibility: Name and details read as one element
Open and download name the file they act on
Rows stack at accessibility text sizes instead of truncating

name: StanceCanvasSplitView
summary: Chat beside a working document: two resizable columns on iPad and a segmented switch between them on iPhone.
accessibility: Each side is a labelled region
The divider is adjustable with VoiceOver and the arrow keys
In compact width a system segmented control replaces the divider

name: StanceToolCallCard
summary: A disclosure card for a single tool run by the assistant, with its input, result, duration and status in words.
example: StanceToolCallCard("Search the web", name: "web.search", status: .complete, input: "{ \"query\": \"FY27 budget\" }", output: "3 results", language: "json", duration: 2)
accessibility: The status is part of the name, such as "Search the web, Complete"
A button with its expanded state
Each status change is announced once

name: StanceStepTimeline
summary: A vertical run of agent steps joined by a line, where the step in progress is called current and details open in place.
example: StanceStepTimeline([StanceAgentStep(id: "1", title: "Read the workbook", status: .complete, duration: 3), StanceAgentStep(id: "2", title: "Compare versions", status: .running)])
accessibility: Rows read "Step 2 of 4" with the status in words
The running step is called current
Status never relies on colour or an icon alone

name: StancePlanChecklist
summary: A proposed plan on a system List: rename, drag to reorder or delete steps, watch progress, then approve or reject it.
example: StancePlanChecklist(items: .constant([StancePlanItem(id: "1", title: "Read the workbook"), StancePlanItem(id: "2", title: "Email finance")]), onApprove: {}, onReject: {})
accessibility: Move up, Move down and Remove are VoiceOver actions on each step
Moves and removals are announced
Progress is stated in words

name: StanceApprovalPrompt
summary: An inline card that stops an agent until you allow or deny an action, stating the risk; a countdown can only deny.
example: StanceApprovalPrompt("Email the summary to finance", description: "Sends one message to 6 people.", risk: .high, onAllow: {}, onDeny: {})
accessibility: Announced once when it appears, with the risk in words
Escape denies; Return never allows a high risk action
Allow and deny confirm with a haptic

name: StancePermissionSheet
summary: A native sheet with a Stance switch for each thing an agent may access; required access stays on and says why.
example: Button("Review access") { isPresented = true }.stancePermissionSheet(isPresented: $isPresented, permissions: .constant([StancePermission(id: "files", title: "Read attached files", isGranted: true, isRequired: true)]))
accessibility: The system sheet with its own dismissal gestures
Each permission is a labelled switch
Required switches are disabled and explained in text

name: StanceAgentStatusPill
summary: A small capsule that names the agent state in words, from idle to failed, and becomes a button when given an action.
accessibility: The state is always text beside the mark
Waiting for you interrupts once; other changes are polite
44pt target when it is a button

name: StanceTaskQueue
summary: A card of agent tasks with a running, queued and finished count, plus pause, resume, cancel and retry on each row.
example: StanceTaskQueue(tasks: [StanceAgentTask(id: "1", title: "Export report", status: .running, progress: 0.4), StanceAgentTask(id: "2", title: "Email finance")], onCancel: { _ in })
accessibility: A count summary sits under the heading
Every action names its task, such as "Cancel Export report"
The same actions are VoiceOver actions on the row

name: StanceSubagentTree
summary: A nested list of the agents a lead agent has delegated to, built on the Stance tree with status words on every row.
example: StanceSubagentTree(nodes: [StanceSubagent(id: "lead", name: "Lead", status: .running, children: [StanceSubagent(id: "writer", name: "Writer", status: .waiting)])], expanded: .constant(["lead"]), selection: $selection)
accessibility: Rows read their level, position and expanded state
The status is part of each row's name
Expand and collapse are VoiceOver actions

name: StanceRunLog
summary: A monospaced, left to right log on a lazy stack that sticks to the newest line until you scroll up, with level chips.
example: StanceRunLog(entries: [StanceLogEntry(id: "1", level: .info, text: "Run started"), StanceLogEntry(id: "2", level: .error, text: "Relay timed out")])
accessibility: Only new errors are announced, never every line
Each line reads its level in words
Copying is announced and confirmed with a haptic

name: StanceDiffReview
summary: A proposed change as plus and minus lines per file, unified on iPhone and split on iPad, decided hunk by hunk or all at once.
example: StanceDiffReview(files: [StanceDiffFile(id: "a", path: "notes.md", hunks: [StanceDiffHunk(id: "a1", lines: [StanceDiffLine(.remove, "Travel is flat."), StanceDiffLine(.add, "Travel is up 8%.")])])], decisions: .constant([:]))
accessibility: Lines read "Added" or "Removed" and show a plus or minus, never colour alone
Each hunk is a group with its own accept and reject
Decisions confirm with a haptic and totals are announced
